newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian airline union wants management to resign.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian airline union wants management to resign.

text.p: Trade unions representing staff of Bulgarian state carrier Balkan Airlines said on Friday they were seeking the resignation of the management, which they blame for the airline's financial crisis.
Maria Ivancheva, a leader of the airline's Podkrepa trade union branch said the national carrier needed a new management to implement a stabilisation programme.
"Nothing has been done for the last two years by the airline's management and we want to see who is responsible for Balkan's critical state," Ivancheva said.

Trade union organisations at the airline staged a protest rally at the airline headquarters on Thursday and delivered letters to the prime minister, the transport minister and the speaker of parliament listing their demands.
They threaten further protest action if nothing is done.

The state-run airline increased its losses in the first half of 1996 by 510 million levs against the same period last year. British consultancy firm KPMG is helping Balkan work out a programme aimed at stabilising its finances.
A Balkan Boeing 767-200 plane leased from Air France was detained on Monday at Paris's Charles de Gaulle airport for unpaid bills.
The International Air Transport Association (IATA) also halted payment of Balkan's bills through the association's clearing house until the carrier paid its IATA fees.
Bulgaria began procedures to privatise the national carrier in 1992 but in January 1995 the Privatisation Agency suspended them, citing a lack of buyers.
